When either spouse withdraws from society of other without reasonable excuse, aggrieved party may apply for restitution.
Burden on Respondent to prove reasonable excuse for withdrawal.

PETITION UNDER SECTION 9 OF THE HINDU MARRIAGE ACT, 1955
FOR RESTITUTION OF CONJUGAL RIGHTS

1. Petitioner and Respondent are Hindus married on DD.MM.YYYY at [place] according to Hindu rites. Marriage certificate Annexure 1.
2. After marriage parties lived together at [matrimonial home] until DD.MM.YYYY.
3. Respondent without any reasonable excuse left matrimonial home on DD.MM.YYYY and has since withdrawn from society of Petitioner.
4. [3-4 paragraphs: What Petitioner did to get Respondent to return. Meetings, calls, messages, letters. What Respondent said or did.]
5. Petitioner unable to understand reason for Respondent's withdrawal. Petitioner has always been loving and caring. Petitioner willing to provide all comforts.
6. Respondent has no reasonable excuse for withdrawal. Conduct is without justification.
7. This petition filed within time. Respondent withdrew on DD.MM.YYYY. Filed within limitation.
8. This Court has jurisdiction — parties last resided together within its territorial jurisdiction.

PRAYER:
